737:     /// LOGPROD / LOGMIN / LOGMAX: Using `prod`/`min`/`max` on logical values.
738:     fn check_logical_aggregation(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
739:         if node.kind() != "function_call" {
740:             return Vec::new();
741:         }
742: 
743:         let func_name = match get_function_call_name(node, source) {
744:             Some(n) => n,
745:             None => return Vec::new(),
746:         };
747: 
748:         let (check_id, replacement) = match func_name {
749:             "prod" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGPROD") => ("LOGPROD", "all"),
750:             "min" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGMIN") => ("LOGMIN", "all"),
751:             "max" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGMAX") => ("LOGMAX", "any"),
752:             _ => return Vec::new(),
753:         };
754: 
755:         // Heuristic: check if the argument is likely logical (named with `is`, `has`,
756:         // or is a comparison result). We can't know types statically, so this is
757:         // limited to obvious patterns.
758:         let args_node = find_child_of_kind(node, "arguments");
759:         let first_arg = args_node.and_then(|a| first_named_child(a));
760:         let looks_logical = first_arg
761:             .map(|arg| {
762:                 let kind = arg.kind();
763:                 if kind == "comparison_operator" || kind == "boolean_operator" {
764:                     return true;
765:                 }
766:                 if kind == "identifier" {
767:                     let name = node_text(arg, source);
768:                     return name.starts_with("is")
769:                         || name.starts_with("has")
770:                         || name == "true"
771:                         || name == "false";
772:                 }
773:                 if kind == "unary_operator" {
774:                     let text = node_text(arg, source);
775:                     return text.starts_with('~');
776:                 }
777:                 false
778:             })
779:             .unwrap_or(false);
780: 
781:         if !looks_logical {
782:             return Vec::new();
783:         }
784: 
785:         let pos = node.start_position();
786:         vec![Diagnostic {
787:             rule_id: check_id,
788:             message: format!(
789:                 "Use {replacement}() instead of {func_name}() for logical arrays"
790:             ),
791:             severity: Severity::Warning,
792:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
793:             line: pos.row + 1,
794:             column: pos.column + 1,
795:             fix: None,
796:         }]
797:     }

1102:     /// PFGP: assignment to a GLOBAL or PERSISTENT variable inside a PARFOR loop.
1103:     fn check_pfgp(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
1104:         if !self.is_check_enabled("PFGP") || !is_parfor_node(node, source) {
1105:             return Vec::new();
1106:         }
1107: 
1108:         let globals = collect_global_persistent_vars(root_node_of(node), source);
1109:         if globals.is_empty() {
1110:             return Vec::new();
1111:         }
1112:         let body = match find_child_of_kind(node, "block") {
1113:             Some(b) => b,
1114:             None => return Vec::new(),
1115:         };
1116: 
1117:         let mut assignments = Vec::new();
1118:         collect_nodes_of_kind(body, "assignment", &mut assignments);
1119:         let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
1120:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
1121:         for assign in assignments {
1122:             let lhs = match assign.child_by_field_name("left") {
1123:                 Some(l) => l,
1124:                 None => continue,
1125:             };
1126:             let name = match lhs_base_name(lhs, source) {
1127:                 Some(n) => n,

1723:     /// CTPCT: `sprintf`/`fprintf` format specifier count does not match the
1724:     /// number of remaining arguments.
1725:     fn check_ctpct(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
1726:         if !self.is_check_enabled("CTPCT") || node.kind() != "function_call" {
1727:             return Vec::new();
1728:         }
1729: 
1730:         let func_name = match get_function_call_name(node, source) {
1731:             Some(n) => n,
1732:             None => return Vec::new(),
1733:         };
1734:         if func_name != "sprintf" && func_name != "fprintf" {
1735:             return Vec::new();
1736:         }
1737: 
1738:         let args_node = match find_child_of_kind(node, "arguments") {
1739:             Some(a) => a,
1740:             None => return Vec::new(),
1741:         };
1742: 
1743:         let mut cursor = args_node.walk();
1744:         let args: Vec<Node> = args_node
1745:             .children(&mut cursor)
1746:             .filter(|c| c.is_named())
1747:             .collect();
1748:         let format_index = match args.iter().position(|a| a.kind() == "string") {
1749:             Some(i) => i,
1750:             None => return Vec::new(),
1751:         };
1752: 
1753:         let fmt_text = node_text(args[format_index], source).trim_matches('\'');
1754:         let specifiers = count_format_specifiers(fmt_text);
1755:         let arg_count = args.len() - format_index - 1;
1756:         if specifiers == arg_count {
1757:             return Vec::new();
1758:         }
1759: 
1760:         let pos = node.start_position();
1761:         vec![Diagnostic {
1762:             rule_id: "CTPCT",
1763:             message: "The format might not agree with the argument count.".to_string(),
1764:             severity: Severity::Warning,
1765:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1766:             line: pos.row + 1,
1767:             column: pos.column + 1,
1768:             fix: None,
1769:         }]
1770:     }

1798:     /// SIMPT: `import` command does not run before any other code in its
1799:     /// enclosing function.
1800:     fn check_simpt(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
1801:         if !self.is_check_enabled("SIMPT") || node.kind() != "command" {
1802:             return Vec::new();
1803:         }
1804:         if get_command_name(node, source) != Some("import") {
1805:             return Vec::new();
1806:         }
1807: 
1808:         // Skip file/script-level imports (no enclosing function).
1809:         let func = match enclosing_function(node) {
1810:             Some(f) => f,
1811:             None => return Vec::new(),
1812:         };
1813:         let block = match find_child_of_kind(func, "block") {
1814:             Some(b) => b,
1815:             None => return Vec::new(),
1816:         };
1817: 
1818:         // Fire unless the import is the first non-comment statement in the block.
1819:         let mut cursor = block.walk();
1820:         let first_stmt = block
1821:             .children(&mut cursor)
1822:             .find(|c| c.is_named() && c.kind() != "comment");
1823:         if let Some(first) = first_stmt {
1824:             if first.start_byte() == node.start_byte() && first.end_byte() == node.end_byte() {
1825:                 return Vec::new();
1826:             }
1827:         }
1828: 
1829:         let func_name = func
1830:             .child_by_field_name("name")
1831:             .map(|n| node_text(n, source))
1832:             .unwrap_or("");
1833: 
1834:         let pos = node.start_position();
1835:         vec![Diagnostic {
1836:             rule_id: "SIMPT",
1837:             message: format!(
1838:                 "This import statement runs before any other code in function {func_name}. Consider placing it at the top of the function body."
1839:             ),
1840:             severity: Severity::Warning,
1841:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1842:             line: pos.row + 1,
1843:             column: pos.column + 1,
1844:             fix: None,

1848:     /// TLEV: dynamic-code function (`eval`/`evalc`/`evalin`/`feval`) used as a
1849:     /// sub-expression rather than a top-level statement.
1850:     fn check_tlev(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
1851:         if !self.is_check_enabled("TLEV") || node.kind() != "function_call" {
1852:             return Vec::new();
1853:         }
1854: 
1855:         let func_name = match get_function_call_name(node, source) {
1856:             Some(n) => n,
1857:             None => return Vec::new(),
1858:         };
1859:         if !["eval", "evalc", "evalin", "feval"].contains(&func_name) {
1860:             return Vec::new();
1861:         }
1862: 
1863:         // A call that is the entire right-hand side of an assignment is still a
1864:         // top-level statement; anything deeper is a sub-expression.
1865:         if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
1866:             if parent.kind() == "assignment" {
1867:                 if let Some(right) = parent.child_by_field_name("right") {
1868:                     if right.start_byte() == node.start_byte()
1869:                         && right.end_byte() == node.end_byte()
1870:                     {
1871:                         return Vec::new();
1872:                     }
1873:                 }
1874:             }
1875:         }
1876: 
1877:         let pos = node.start_position();
1878:         vec![Diagnostic {
1879:             rule_id: "TLEV",
1880:             message: format!(
1881:                 "{func_name} could be very inefficient unless it is a top-level statement in its function."
1882:             ),
1883:             severity: Severity::Warning,
1884:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1885:             line: pos.row + 1,
1886:             column: pos.column + 1,
1887:             fix: None,
1888:         }]
1889:     }

2071:     /// STRSZ: `==`/`~=` between string literals of different sizes.
2072:     fn check_strsz(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
2073:         if !self.is_check_enabled("STRSZ") {
2074:             return Vec::new();
2075:         }
2076:         if node.kind() != "comparison_operator" && node.kind() != "binary_operator" {
2077:             return Vec::new();
2078:         }
2079: 
2080:         let text = node_text(node, source);
2081:         if !text.contains("==") && !text.contains("~=") {
2082:             return Vec::new();
2083:         }
2084: 
2085:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
2086:         let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
2087:         let op_idx = match children
2088:             .iter()
2089:             .position(|c| c.kind() == "==" || c.kind() == "~=")
2090:         {
2091:             Some(i) if i > 0 && i + 1 < children.len() => i,
2092:             _ => return Vec::new(),
2093:         };
2094: 
2095:         let left = children[op_idx - 1];
2096:         let right = children[op_idx + 1];
2097:         if left.kind() != "string" || right.kind() != "string" {
2098:             return Vec::new();
2099:         }
2100:         if node_text(left, source).len() == node_text(right, source).len() {
2101:             return Vec::new();
2102:         }
2103: 
2104:         let pos = node.start_position();
2105:         vec![Diagnostic {
2106:             rule_id: "STRSZ",
2107:             message: "Use STRCMP to compare character vectors that can have different sizes."
2108:                 .to_string(),
2109:             severity: Severity::Warning,
2110:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
2111:             line: pos.row + 1,
2112:             column: pos.column + 1,
2113:             fix: None,
2114:         }]
2115:     }

2148:     /// COMPNOP: `call(...) == true` simplifies to `call(...)`.
2149:     fn check_compnop(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {

2151:             return Vec::new();
2152:         }
2153: 
2154:         let Some((call_node, literal_node, op)) = self.comparison_with_literal(node, source) else {
2155:             return Vec::new();
2156:         };
2157:         let literal = node_text(literal_node, source).trim();
2158:         if op != "==" || literal != "true" {
2159:             return Vec::new();
2160:         }
2161: 
2162:         let call_text = node_text(call_node, source).to_string();
2163:         let func_name = get_function_call_name(call_node, source).unwrap_or("function");
2164:         let pos = node.start_position();
2165:         vec![Diagnostic {
2166:             rule_id: "COMPNOP",
2167:             message: format!(
2168:                 "This logical comparison simplifies to {call_text}. Did you mean to use {func_name} to evaluate function argument: {call_text}?"
2169:             ),
2170:             severity: Severity::Warning,
2171:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
2172:             line: pos.row + 1,
2173:             column: pos.column + 1,
2174:             fix: Some(Fix::new(
2175:                 node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
2176:                 call_text,
2177:             )),
2178:         }]

2181:     /// COMPNOT: `call(...) ~= true` or `call(...) == false` simplifies to
2182:     /// `~call(...)`.
2183:     fn check_comnot(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
2184:         if !self.is_check_enabled("COMPNOT") || node.kind() != "comparison_operator" {

2186:         }

2188:         let Some((call_node, literal_node, op)) = self.comparison_with_literal(node, source) else {

2190:         };

2193:         if !is_comnot {

2197:         let call_text = node_text(call_node, source).to_string();

2199:         let pos = node.start_position();
2200:         vec![Diagnostic {
2201:             rule_id: "COMPNOT",
2202:             message: format!(
2203:                 "This logical comparison simplifies to ~{call_text}. Did you mean to use {func_name} to evaluate function argument: {call_text}?"
2204:             ),
2205:             severity: Severity::Warning,
2206:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
2207:             line: pos.row + 1,
2208:             column: pos.column + 1,
2209:             fix: Some(Fix::new(

2216:     /// Shared COMPNOP/COMPNOT logic: extract the `(call, literal, operator)`
2217:     /// triple from a `comparison_operator` node when exactly one operand is a
2218:     /// `function_call` and the other is the `true`/`false` literal.
2219:     fn comparison_with_literal<'a>(
2220:         &self,
2221:         node: Node<'a>,
2222:         source: &'a str,
2223:     ) -> Option<(Node<'a>, Node<'a>, String)> {
2224:         let lhs = node.child(0)?;
2225:         let rhs = node.child(2)?;
2226:         let op = find_operator_text(node, source);
2227: 
2228:         let (call_node, literal_node) = match (lhs.kind(), rhs.kind()) {
2229:             ("function_call", "identifier") => (lhs, rhs),
2230:             ("identifier", "function_call") => (rhs, lhs),
2231:             _ => return None,
2232:         };
2233:         let literal = node_text(literal_node, source).trim();
2234:         if literal == "true" || literal == "false" {
2235:             Some((call_node, literal_node, op))
2236:         } else {
2237:             None
2238:         }
2239:     }

2241:     /// M3COL: an expression with three colons (`a:b:c:d`) is probably
2242:     /// unintended. The grammar cannot represent four-element colon chains, so
2243:     /// they parse as a `range` plus a trailing ERROR node (or a range nested
2244:     /// inside an ERROR node); all three shapes are detected here.
2245:     fn check_m3col(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
2246:         if !self.is_check_enabled("M3COL") || node.kind() != "range" {
2247:             return Vec::new();
2248:         }
2249: 
2250:         let mut colon_count = node_text(node, source).matches(':').count();
2251:         let mut end_byte = node.end_byte();
2252: 
2253:         if let Some(next) = node.next_named_sibling() {
2254:             if next.kind() == "ERROR" && node_text(next, source).starts_with(':') {
2255:                 colon_count += node_text(next, source).matches(':').count();
2256:                 end_byte = end_byte.max(next.end_byte());
2257:             }
2258:         }
2259:         if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
2260:             if parent.kind() == "ERROR" {
2261:                 colon_count += node_text(parent, source).matches(':').count();
2262:                 end_byte = end_byte.max(parent.end_byte());
2263:             } else if let Some(next) = parent.next_named_sibling() {
2264:                 if next.kind() == "ERROR" && node_text(next, source).starts_with(':') {
2265:                     colon_count += node_text(next, source).matches(':').count();
2266:                     end_byte = end_byte.max(next.end_byte());
2267:                 }
2268:             }
2269:         }
2270: 
2271:         if colon_count < 3 {
2272:             return Vec::new();
2273:         }
2274: 
2275:         let pos = node.start_position();
2276:         vec![Diagnostic {
2277:             rule_id: "M3COL",
2278:             message: "Using three colons (a:b:c:d) in an expression is probably unintended"
2279:                 .to_string(),
2280:             severity: Severity::Warning,
2281:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..end_byte,
2282:             line: pos.row + 1,
2283:             column: pos.column + 1,
2284:             fix: None,
2285:         }]
2286:     }

2880:             if self.is_check_enabled("PFIIN") {
2881:                 if let Some(body_node) = body {
2882:                     let mut skip = std::collections::HashSet::new();
2883:                     if let Some(ref idx) = idx_var {
2884:                         skip.insert(idx.clone());
2885:                     }
2886:                     let reads = collect_parfor_body_reads(body_node, source, &skip);
2887:                     for (name, read_node) in reads {
2888:                         if is_defined_before_parfor(&sym, &name, parfor.start_byte())
2889:                             || is_assigned_in_body(body_node, &name, source)
2890:                         {
2891:                             continue;
2892:                         }
2893:                         let pos = read_node.start_position();
2894:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
2895:                             rule_id: "PFIIN",
2896:                             message: format!(
2897:                                 "The input variable {name} should be initialized before the PARFOR loop."
2898:                             ),
2899:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
2900:                             byte_range: read_node.start_byte()..read_node.end_byte(),
2901:                             line: pos.row + 1,
2902:                             column: pos.column + 1,
2903:                             fix: None,
2904:                         });
2905:                     }
2906:                 }
2907:             }
2908: 
2909:             // PFOUS / PFTUSW: simple-identifier assignments in the body and
2910:             // whether the variable is used after the loop.
2911:             let need_assignments = self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS") || self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW");
2912:             if need_assignments {
2913:                 if let Some(body_node) = body {
2914:                     let assigned = collect_simple_lhs_assignments(body_node, source);
2915:                     for (name, lhs_node) in assigned {
2916:                         if idx_var.as_deref() == Some(name.as_str()) {
2917:                             continue;
2918:                         }
2919:                         let uses =
2920:                             uses_after_parfor(&sym, &name, parfor.end_byte(), tree, false);
2921:                         if self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS") && uses.is_empty() {
2922:                             let pos = lhs_node.start_position();
2923:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
2924:                                 rule_id: "PFOUS",
2925:                                 message: format!(
2926:                                     "The output variable {name} might not be used after the PARFOR loop."
2927:                                 ),
2928:                                 severity: Severity::Warning,
2929:                                 byte_range: lhs_node.start_byte()..lhs_node.end_byte(),
2930:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
2931:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
2932:                                 fix: None,
2933:                             });
2934:                         }
2935:                         if self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW") {
2936:                             if let Some(line) = uses.first() {
2937:                                 let pos = lhs_node.start_position();
2938:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
2939:                                     rule_id: "PFTUSW",
2940:                                     message: format!(
2941:                                         "The temporary variable {name} might be used after the PARFOR loop on line {line}."
2942:                                     ),
2943:                                     severity: Severity::Warning,

2945:                                     line: pos.row + 1,

2951:                     }
2952:                 }
2953:             }
2954: 
2955:             // PFUIXW: index variable used after the loop.
2956:             if self.is_check_enabled("PFUIXW") {
2957:                 if let Some(ref idx) = idx_var {
2958:                     let uses = uses_after_parfor(&sym, idx, parfor.end_byte(), tree, true);
2959:                     if let Some(line) = uses.first() {
2960:                         let idx_node = find_parfor_index_identifier(*parfor);
2961:                         let target = idx_node.unwrap_or(*parfor);
2962:                         let pos = target.start_position();
2963:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
2964:                             rule_id: "PFUIXW",
2965:                             message: format!(
2966:                                 "The index variable {idx} might be used after the PARFOR loop on line {line}."
2967:                             ),
2968:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
2969:                             byte_range: target.start_byte()..target.end_byte(),
2970:                             line: pos.row + 1,
2971:                             column: pos.column + 1,
2972:                             fix: None,
2973:                         });
2974:                     }
2975:                 }
2976:             }
2977:         }
2978: 
2979:         diagnostics

3221: fn find_operator_text<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> String {
3222:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3223:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
3224:         if !child.is_named() {

3227:             if !trimmed.is_empty()
3228:                 && trimmed != "("
3229:                 && trimmed != ")"
3230:                 && trimmed != ","
3231:             {
3232:                 return trimmed.to_string();
3233:             }
3234:         }
3235:     }
3236: 
3237:     if let Some(op_node) = node.child_by_field_name("operator") {
3238:         return node_text(op_node, source).trim().to_string();
3239:     }
3240: 
3241:     let text = node_text(node, source);
3242:     for op in &["==", "~=", ">=", "<=", "&&", "||", ">", "<", "&", "|", "+", "-", "*", "/", "^"] {
3243:         if text.contains(op) {

3245:         }
3246:     }

3248:     String::new()

3267: /// Classify the type of eval usage based on argument text patterns.
3268: fn classify_eval_usage(args_text: &str, config: &GoodPracticesConfig) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
3269:     // EVLDOT: dynamic field access patterns like `eval(['s.' fieldname])`
3270:     if (args_text.contains("s.") || args_text.contains(".("))
3271:         && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLDOT")
3272:     {
3273:         return (
3274:             "EVLDOT",
3275:             "Avoid eval() for dynamic field access; use s.(fieldname) instead",
3276:         );
3277:     }
3278: 
3279:     // EVLSYS: system command patterns
3280:     if (args_text.contains("system") || args_text.contains("dos") || args_text.contains("unix"))
3281:         && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLSYS")
3282:     {
3283:         return (
3284:             "EVLSYS",
3285:             "Avoid eval() for system commands; use system() directly",
3286:         );
3287:     }
3288: 
3289:     // EVLEQ: dynamic variable creation like `eval([varname ' = ...'])`
3290:     if args_text.contains(" = ") && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLEQ") {
3291:         return (
3292:             "EVLEQ",

3294:         );
3295:     }
3296: 
3297:     // EVLSEQVAR: sequential variable creation like `eval(['x' num2str(i)])`
3298:     if (args_text.contains("num2str") || args_text.contains("int2str"))
3299:         && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLSEQVAR")
3300:     {
3301:         return (
3302:             "EVLSEQVAR",
3303:             "Avoid eval() to create sequential variables; use cell arrays or struct fields",
3304:         );

3308:     (
3309:         "EVLCS",
3310:         "Avoid eval(); it is slow, hard to debug, and a security risk",

3373: /// Find element-wise boolean operators (`&`, `|`) in if/while conditions.
3374: fn find_element_wise_boolean_in_condition(
3375:     node: Node,
3376:     source: &str,
3377:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
3378: ) {
3379:     // The condition of if/while is typically the first expression child.
3380:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3381:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
3382:         if child.kind() == "boolean_operator" {
3383:             let text = node_text(child, source);
3384:             // Single `&` or `|` (not `&&` or `||`)
3385:             let has_element_wise =
3386:                 (text.contains('&') && !text.contains("&&"))
3387:                     || (text.contains('|') && !text.contains("||"));
3388:             if has_element_wise {
3389:                 let pos = child.start_position();
3390:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
3391:                     rule_id: "ELARLOG",
3392:                     message: "Use short-circuit operators (&&, ||) instead of element-wise (&, |) in if/while conditions".to_string(),
3393:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
3394:                     byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
3395:                     line: pos.row + 1,
3396:                     column: pos.column + 1,
3397:                     fix: None,
3398:                 });
3399:             }
3400:         }
3401:         // Don't recurse into nested if/while/for/blocks — just check immediate condition.
3402:         if child.kind() == "block" || child.kind() == "elseif_clause" || child.kind() == "else_clause" {
3403:             continue;
3404:         }
3405:         find_element_wise_boolean_in_condition(child, source, diagnostics);
3406:     }
3407: }

3409: /// Find the function_definition node overlapping a byte range.
3410: fn find_node_in_range<'a>(root: Node<'a>, range: &std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
3411:     if root.kind() == "function_definition"
3412:         && root.start_byte() == range.start
3413:         && root.end_byte() == range.end
3414:     {
3415:         return Some(root);
3416:     }
3417:     let mut cursor = root.walk();
3418:     for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
3419:         if child.start_byte() > range.end || child.end_byte() < range.start {
3420:             continue;
3421:         }
3422:         if let Some(found) = find_node_in_range(child, range) {
3423:             return Some(found);
3424:         }
3425:     }
3426:     None
3427: }

3429: /// Collect statements grouped by line number (for SEPEX).
3430: fn collect_statements_by_line(
3431:     node: Node,
3432:     line_statements: &mut std::collections::HashMap<usize, Vec<(usize, usize)>>,
3433: ) {
3434:     let kind = node.kind();
3435: 
3436:     // Only collect at statement level in source_file or block.
3437:     if kind == "source_file" || kind == "block" {
3438:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
3439:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
3440:             let ck = child.kind();
3441:             if ck == ";"
3442:                 || ck == ","
3443:                 || ck == "comment"
3444:                 || ck == "end"
3445:                 || ck == "line_continuation"
3446:                 || !child.is_named()
3447:             {
3448:                 continue;
3449:             }
3450:             let line = child.start_position().row + 1;
3451:             line_statements
3452:                 .entry(line)
3453:                 .or_default()
3454:                 .push((child.start_byte(), child.end_byte()));
3455:         }
3456:     }
3457: 
3458:     // Recurse into structural nodes.
3459:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3460:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
3461:         let ck = child.kind();
3462:         if ck == "block"
3463:             || ck == "function_definition"
3464:             || ck == "if_statement"
3465:             || ck == "for_statement"
3466:             || ck == "while_statement"
3467:             || ck == "switch_statement"
3468:             || ck == "try_statement"
3469:             || ck == "catch_clause"
3470:             || ck == "methods"
3471:             || ck == "class_definition"
3472:         {
3473:             collect_statements_by_line(child, line_statements);
3474:         }
3475:     }
3476: }

3478: /// Find `end` used as an index argument (FNCOLND).
3479: fn find_end_as_index(node: Node, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
3480:     if node.kind() == "end" {
3481:         // Check if parent is an indexing context (function_call arguments).
3482:         if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
3483:             if parent.kind() == "arguments" {
3484:                 // Check if grandparent is a function_call (which could be indexing).
3485:                 if let Some(gp) = parent.parent() {
3486:                     if gp.kind() == "function_call" {
3487:                         // Count the number of argument separators (commas) to determine
3488:                         // if this is a multi-dimensional index. `end` without explicit
3489:                         // dimension is fine for 1-D indexing but ambiguous for multi-D.
3490:                         let comma_count = count_children_of_kind(parent, ",");
3491:                         if comma_count > 0 {
3492:                             let pos = node.start_position();
3493:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
3494:                                 rule_id: "FNCOLND",
3495:                                 message: "'end' used in multi-dimensional indexing; specify the dimension explicitly".to_string(),
3496:                                 severity: Severity::Warning,
3497:                                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
3498:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
3499:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
3500:                                 fix: None,
3501:                             });
3502:                         }
3503:                     }
3504:                 }
3505:             }
3506:         }
3507:     }
3508: 
3509:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3510:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
3511:         find_end_as_index(child, diagnostics);
3512:     }
3513: }

3515: /// Count children of a specific kind.
3516: fn count_children_of_kind(node: Node, kind: &str) -> usize {
3517:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3518:     node.children(&mut cursor)
3519:         .filter(|c| c.kind() == kind)
3520:         .count()
3521: }

3527: /// Get the root node of a tree by walking up from a node.
3528: fn root_node_of<'a>(mut node: Node<'a>) -> Node<'a> {
3529:     while let Some(p) = node.parent() {
3530:         node = p;
3531:     }
3532:     node
3533: }

3535: /// Check whether a `for_statement` node is a parfor loop.
3536: fn is_parfor_node(node: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
3537:     node.kind() == "for_statement" && node_text(node, source).trim_start().starts_with("parfor")
3538: }

3540: /// Count the named children of a node.
3541: fn count_named_children(node: Node) -> usize {
3542:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3543:     node.children(&mut cursor).filter(|c| c.is_named()).count()
3544: }

3546: /// Get the `range` node of a for/parfor statement's iterator.

3548:     let iter = find_child_of_kind(node, "iterator")?;
3549:     find_child_of_kind(iter, "range")

3552: /// Get the last named child of a node (including `end`).
3553: fn last_named_child(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
3554:     let mut result = None;
3555:     let count = node.child_count();
3556:     for i in 0..count {
3557:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
3558:             if child.is_named() {
3559:                 result = Some(child);
3560:             }
3561:         }
3562:     }

3566: /// Extract the parfor index variable name.

3569: }

3571: /// Find the parfor index variable identifier node.
3572: fn find_parfor_index_identifier(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
3573:     let iter = find_child_of_kind(node, "iterator")?;
3574:     let count = iter.child_count();
3575:     for i in 0..count {
3576:         if let Some(c) = iter.child(i) {
3577:             if c.kind() == "identifier" {
3578:                 return Some(c);
3579:             }
3580:         }
3581:     }
3582:     None

3585: /// Walk a node collecting all `function_call` and `command` descendants.
3586: fn walk_body_for_function_calls<'a>(node: Node<'a>, out: &mut Vec<Node<'a>>) {
3587:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3588:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
3589:         if child.kind() == "function_call" || child.kind() == "command" {
3590:             out.push(child);
3591:         }
3592:         if child.is_named() {
3593:             walk_body_for_function_calls(child, out);
3594:         }
3595:     }
3596: }

3598: /// Collect all descendants of a node with the given kind.
3599: fn collect_nodes_of_kind<'a>(node: Node<'a>, kind: &str, out: &mut Vec<Node<'a>>) {
3600:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
3601:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
3602:         if child.kind() == kind {
3603:             out.push(child);
3604:         }
3605:         if child.is_named() {
3606:             collect_nodes_of_kind(child, kind, out);
3607:         }
3608:     }
3609: }

3611: /// Collect all parfor `for_statement` nodes in a tree.
3612: fn collect_parfor_nodes<'a>(root: Node<'a>, source: &str) -> Vec<Node<'a>> {
3613:     let mut out = Vec::new();
3614:     if is_parfor_node(root, source) {
3615:         out.push(root);
3616:     }
3617:     let mut cursor = root.walk();
3618:     for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
3619:         if child.is_named() {
3620:             out.extend(collect_parfor_nodes(child, source));
3621:         }
3622:     }
3623:     out
3624: }

3626: /// Collect all identifiers declared `global` or `persistent` anywhere in a tree.
3627: fn collect_global_persistent_vars(root: Node, source: &str) -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {
3628:     let mut vars = std::collections::HashSet::new();
3629:     let mut cursor = root.walk();
3630:     for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
3631:         if child.kind() == "global_operator" || child.kind() == "persistent_operator" {
3632:             let mut c2 = child.walk();
3633:             for id in child.children(&mut c2) {
3634:                 if id.kind() == "identifier" {
3635:                     vars.insert(node_text(id, source).to_string());
3636:                 }
3637:             }
3638:         }
3639:         if child.is_named() {
3640:             vars.extend(collect_global_persistent_vars(child, source));
3641:         }
3642:     }
3643:     vars
3644: }

3646: /// Check whether a function call / command is `evalin`/`assignin` with `'base'`.
3647: fn is_evalin_assignin_base(node: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
3648:     let func_name = match node.kind() {
3649:         "function_call" => get_function_call_name(node, source),
3650:         "command" => get_command_name(node, source),
3651:         _ => return false,
3652:     };
3653:     let func_name = match func_name {
3654:         Some(n) => n,
3655:         None => return false,
3656:     };
3657:     if func_name != "evalin" && func_name != "assignin" {
3658:         return false;
3659:     }
3660: 
3661:     let first_arg = if node.kind() == "function_call" {
3662:         find_child_of_kind(node, "arguments").and_then(|a| first_named_child(a))
3663:     } else {
3664:         find_child_of_kind(node, "command_argument")
3665:     };
3666:     let first_arg = match first_arg {
3667:         Some(a) => a,
3668:         None => return false,
3669:     };
3670:     let text = node_text(first_arg, source).trim();
3671:     let text = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
3672:     text == "base"
3673: }
3674: 
3675: /// Check whether a function call / command constructs a distributed array.
3676: fn is_distributed_call(node: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
3677:     let func_name = match node.kind() {
3678:         "function_call" => get_function_call_name(node, source),
3679:         "command" => get_command_name(node, source),
3680:         _ => return false,
3681:     };
3682:     matches!(
3683:         func_name,
3684:         Some("distributed") | Some("gpuArray") | Some("codistributed")
3685:     )
3686: }

3688: /// Extract the base variable name assigned by an assignment LHS.
3689: fn lhs_base_name(lhs: Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
3690:     match lhs.kind() {
3691:         "identifier" => Some(node_text(lhs, source).to_string()),
3692:         "function_call" => get_function_call_name(lhs, source).map(|s| s.to_string()),
3693:         "field_expression" => find_child_of_kind(lhs, "identifier")
3694:             .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string()),
3695:         _ => None,
3696:     }

3699: /// Emit use-of-global diagnostics for a body node (PFGV / SPGV).
3700: ///
3701: /// When `skip_writes` is true, assignment LHS identifiers are excluded
3702: /// (they are handled by the separate PFGP check).
3703: fn collect_global_use_diagnostics<'a>(
3704:     body: Node<'a>,
3705:     source: &str,
3706:     globals: &std::collections::HashSet<String>,
3707:     rule_id: &'static str,
3708:     skip_writes: bool,
3709: ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
3710:     let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
3711:     let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
3712:     let mut identifiers = Vec::new();
3713:     collect_nodes_of_kind(body, "identifier", &mut identifiers);
3714:     for id in identifiers {
3715:         let name = node_text(id, source).to_string();
3716:         if !globals.contains(&name) {
3717:             continue;
3718:         }
3719:         if let Some(parent) = id.parent() {
3720:             match parent.kind() {
3721:                 "global_operator" | "persistent_operator" => continue,
3722:                 "assignment" => {
3723:                     if skip_writes
3724:                         && parent
3725:                             .child_by_field_name("left")
3726:                             .map(|l| l.id() == id.id())
3727:                             .unwrap_or(false)
3728:                     {
3729:                         continue;
3730:                     }
3731:                 }
3732:                 "field_expression" => {
3733:                     if parent
3734:                         .child_by_field_name("field")
3735:                         .map(|f| f.id() == id.id())
3736:                         .unwrap_or(false)
3737:                     {
3738:                         continue;
3739:                     }
3740:                 }
3741:                 _ => {}
3742:             }
3743:         }
3744:         if !seen.insert(name.clone()) {
3745:             continue;
3746:         }
3747:         let pos = id.start_position();
3748:         let message = if rule_id == "PFGV" {
3749:             format!("Avoid using GLOBAL variable {name} in a PARFOR loop.")
3750:         } else {
3751:             format!(
3752:                 "Using the GLOBAL or PERSISTENT variable {name} in an SPMD block might fail because it is accessed on a worker machine."
3753:             )
3754:         };
3755:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
3756:             rule_id,
3757:             message,
3758:             severity: Severity::Warning,
3759:             byte_range: id.start_byte()..id.end_byte(),
3760:             line: pos.row + 1,
3761:             column: pos.column + 1,
3762:             fix: None,
3763:         });
3764:     }
3765:     diagnostics
3766: }

3768: /// Collect plain-identifier reads inside a parfor body (for PFIIN).
3769: ///
3770: /// Function-call names, assignment LHS writes, field names, and declarations
3771: /// are excluded; only genuine variable reads are returned, deduplicated by name.
3772: fn collect_parfor_body_reads<'a>(
3773:     node: Node<'a>,
3774:     source: &str,
3775:     skip: &std::collections::HashSet<String>,
3776: ) -> Vec<(String, Node<'a>)> {
3777:     let mut out = Vec::new();
3778:     let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
3779:     let mut identifiers = Vec::new();
3780:     collect_nodes_of_kind(node, "identifier", &mut identifiers);
3781:     for id in identifiers {
3782:         let name = node_text(id, source).to_string();
3783:         if skip.contains(&name) {
3784:             continue;
3785:         }
3786:         if let Some(parent) = id.parent() {
3787:             match parent.kind() {
3788:                 "function_call" => {
3789:                     if parent
3790:                         .child_by_field_name("name")
3791:                         .map(|n| n.id() == id.id())
3792:                         .unwrap_or(false)
3793:                     {
3794:                         continue;
3795:                     }
3796:                 }
3797:                 "assignment" => {
3798:                     if parent
3799:                         .child_by_field_name("left")
3800:                         .map(|l| l.id() == id.id())
3801:                         .unwrap_or(false)
3802:                     {
3803:                         continue;
3804:                     }
3805:                 }
3806:                 "global_operator" | "persistent_operator" => continue,
3807:                 "field_expression" => {
3808:                     if parent
3809:                         .child_by_field_name("field")
3810:                         .map(|f| f.id() == id.id())
3811:                         .unwrap_or(false)
3812:                     {
3813:                         continue;
3814:                     }
3815:                 }
3816:                 "iterator" => continue,
3817:                 _ => {}
3818:             }
3819:         }
3820:         if seen.insert(name.clone()) {
3821:             out.push((name, id));
3822:         }
3823:     }
3824:     out
3825: }

3827: /// Collect simple-identifier LHS assignments inside a node (for PFOUS/PFTUSW).
3828: fn collect_simple_lhs_assignments<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &str) -> Vec<(String, Node<'a>)> {
3829:     let mut out = Vec::new();
3830:     let mut assignments = Vec::new();
3831:     collect_nodes_of_kind(node, "assignment", &mut assignments);
3832:     for assign in assignments {
3833:         if let Some(lhs) = assign.child_by_field_name("left") {
3834:             if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
3835:                 out.push((node_text(lhs, source).to_string(), lhs));
3836:             }
3837:         }
3838:     }
3839:     out
3840: }

3842: /// Check whether a variable is assigned anywhere inside a node.
3843: fn is_assigned_in_body(node: Node, name: &str, source: &str) -> bool {
3844:     collect_simple_lhs_assignments(node, source)
3845:         .iter()
3846:         .any(|(n, _)| n == name)

3849: /// Check whether a variable is defined before a parfor loop starts.
3850: ///
3851: /// Function inputs and global/persistent declarations always count as defined;
3852: /// other definitions count if their byte range ends before the loop.
3853: fn is_defined_before_parfor(sym: &SymbolTable, name: &str, parfor_start: usize) -> bool {
3854:     sym.scopes.iter().any(|s| {
3855:         s.defs.iter().any(|d| {
3856:             d.name == name
3857:                 && (matches!(
3858:                     d.kind,
3859:                     crate::analysis::symbols::DefKind::InputArg
3860:                         | crate::analysis::symbols::DefKind::Global
3861:                         | crate::analysis::symbols::DefKind::Persistent
3862:                 ) || d.byte_range.end <= parfor_start)
3863:         })
3864:     })
3865: }

3867: /// Collect lines where a variable is used after a byte offset.
3868: ///
3869: /// When `exclude_loops` is true, uses inside any enclosing `for_statement`
3870: /// are ignored (the variable is re-bound by a subsequent loop).
3871: fn uses_after_parfor(
3872:     sym: &SymbolTable,
3873:     name: &str,
3874:     after: usize,
3875:     tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
3876:     exclude_loops: bool,
3877: ) -> Vec<usize> {
3878:     let mut lines = Vec::new();
3879:     for scope in &sym.scopes {
3880:         for u in &scope.uses {
3881:             if u.name != name || u.byte_range.start < after {
3882:                 continue;
3883:             }
3884:             if exclude_loops {
3885:                 if let Some(n) = tree
3886:                     .root_node()
3887:                     .descendant_for_byte_range(u.byte_range.start, u.byte_range.end)
3888:                 {
3889:                     if is_inside_loop(n) {
3890:                         continue;
3891:                     }
3892:                 }
3893:             }
3894:             lines.push(u.line);
3895:         }
3896:     }
3897:     lines.sort_unstable();
3898:     lines.dedup();
3899:     lines
3900: }

3930: /// Count `printf`-style format specifiers in a format string (for CTPCT).
3931: ///
3932: /// Counts `%` followed by a conversion character. Escaped `%%`, `%*` width
3933: /// specifiers, and `%n$` positional specifiers are not counted.
3934: fn count_format_specifiers(fmt: &str) -> usize {
3935:     let chars: Vec<char> = fmt.chars().collect();
3936:     let mut count = 0;
3937:     let mut i = 0;
3938:     while i < chars.len() {
3939:         if chars[i] != '%' {
3940:             i += 1;
3941:             continue;
3942:         }
3943:         let j = i + 1;
3944:         if j >= chars.len() {
3945:             break;
3946:         }
3947:         if chars[j] == '%' {
3948:             i = j + 1;
3949:             continue;
3950:         }
3951:         if chars[j] == '*' {
3952:             let mut k = j + 1;
3953:             while k < chars.len() && !chars[k].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
3954:                 k += 1;
3955:             }
3956:             i = k + 1;
3957:             continue;
3958:         }
3959:         let mut k = j;
3960:         while k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_digit() {
3961:             k += 1;
3962:         }
3963:         if k < chars.len() && chars[k] == '$' {
3964:             let mut m = k + 1;
3965:             while m < chars.len() && !chars[m].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
3966:                 m += 1;
3967:             }
3968:             i = m + 1;
3969:             continue;
3970:         }
3971:         while k < chars.len() && "-+ #0".contains(chars[k]) {
3972:             k += 1;
3973:         }
3974:         while k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_digit() {
3975:             k += 1;
3976:         }
3977:         if k < chars.len() && chars[k] == '.' {
3978:             k += 1;
3979:             while k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_digit() {
3980:                 k += 1;
3981:             }
3982:         }
3983:         if k < chars.len() && chars[k].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
3984:             count += 1;
3985:             i = k + 1;
3986:         } else {
3987:             i = j;
3988:         }
3989:     }
3990:     count
3991: }

3993: /// Collect assignments to `var_name` inside a loop body, without descending
3994: /// into nested function definitions or anonymous functions (for FXSET).
3995: fn collect_loop_assignments(
3996:     node: Node,
3997:     var_name: &str,
3998:     source: &str,
3999:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
4000: ) {
4001:     if node.kind() == "function_definition" || node.kind() == "lambda" {
4002:         return;
4003:     }
4004:     if node.kind() == "assignment" {
4005:         if let Some(left) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
4006:             if left.kind() == "identifier" && node_text(left, source) == var_name {
4007:                 let pos = node.start_position();
4008:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
4009:                     rule_id: "FXSET",
4010:                     message: format!("Loop index {var_name} is changed inside of a FOR loop."),
4011:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
4012:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
4013:                     line: pos.row + 1,
4014:                     column: pos.column + 1,
4015:                     fix: None,
4016:                 });
4017:             }
4018:         }
4019:     }
4020:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
4021:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
4022:         collect_loop_assignments(child, var_name, source, diagnostics);
4023:     }
4024: }

4026: /// Find the `attribute` node with the given name inside a node that has an
4027: /// `attributes` child (e.g., `class_definition` or a `properties` block).
4028: fn find_attribute_node<'a>(node: Node<'a>, name: &str, source: &'a str) -> Option<Node<'a>> {

4030:     let count = attrs.child_count();
4031:     for i in 0..count {

4033:         if child.kind() != "attribute" {

4036:         if find_child_of_kind(child, "identifier")

4053:     _source: &str,

4058:             bn.start_byte(),
4059:             bn.end_byte(),
4060:             bn.start_position().row + 1,
4061:             bn.start_position().column + 1,
4062:         ),
4063:         None => (class.byte_range.start, class.byte_range.end, class.line, 1),

4794:     /// Collect rule IDs from every node in the subtree, dispatching through the
4795:     /// engine's public `check` entry point.
4796:     fn collect_diagnostics(
4797:         eng: &GoodPracticesEngine,
4798:         node: Node,
4799:         source: &str,
4800:         ids: &mut Vec<&'static str>,
4801:     ) {
4802:         let ctx = NodeContext {
4803:             node,
4804:             source,
4805:             file_path: std::path::Path::new("test.m"),
4806:         };
4807:         ids.extend(eng.check(&ctx).iter().map(|d| d.rule_id));
4808:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
4809:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
4810:             collect_diagnostics(eng, child, source, ids);
4811:         }
4812:     }

4814:     /// Find all descendant nodes of the given kind.
4815:     fn all_descendants_of_kind<'a>(node: Node<'a>, kind: &str) -> Vec<Node<'a>> {
4816:         let mut result = Vec::new();
4817:         if node.kind() == kind {
4818:             result.push(node);
4819:         }
4820:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
4821:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
4822:             result.extend(all_descendants_of_kind(child, kind));
4823:         }
4824:         result
4825:     }

5539:     /// G4 helper: find the first `function_call` descendant with the given name.
5540:     fn goodprac_g4_find_call<'a>(node: Node<'a>, name: &str, source: &'a str) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
5541:         if node.kind() == "function_call" && get_function_call_name(node, source) == Some(name) {
5542:             return Some(node);
5543:         }
5544:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
5545:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
5546:             if let Some(found) = goodprac_g4_find_call(child, name, source) {
5547:                 return Some(found);
5548:             }
5549:         }
5550:         None
5551:     }

5561:     /// Run the full engine (node-level + file-level) and collect rule IDs.
5562:     fn g2_collect_ids(
5563:         eng: &GoodPracticesEngine,
5564:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
5565:         source: &str,
5566:     ) -> Vec<&'static str> {
5567:         let mut ids = Vec::new();
5568:         let mut stack = vec![tree.root_node()];
5569:         while let Some(n) = stack.pop() {
5570:             let ctx = NodeContext {
5571:                 node: n,
5572:                 source,
5573:                 file_path: std::path::Path::new("test.m"),
5574:             };
5575:             ids.extend(eng.check(&ctx).iter().map(|d| d.rule_id));
5576:             let mut cursor = n.walk();
5577:             for c in n.children(&mut cursor) {
5578:                 stack.push(c);
5579:             }
5580:         }
5581:         let fc = FileContext {
5582:             tree,
5583:             source,
5584:             file_path: std::path::Path::new("test.m"),
5585:         };
5586:         ids.extend(eng.check_file(&fc).iter().map(|d| d.rule_id));
5587:         ids
5588:     }
